verdictRationale: Approved. The source is now verified from its own bytes: SHA-256 recomputed against the digest pinned in this family's committed source-record.json, byte length matched, and the visible 'AOC-CR-287, Rev. 12/25' on the source agrees with the pinned REV-2025-12. The source carries no widget value and none of the fixture facts, so it is a genuine blank form. The artifact is correct: six bound values, every one inside the rectangle its own map declares, no stray or duplicated value anywhere in the document, nothing clipped, flattened with no XFA, JavaScript or actions, page 2 word-for-word identical to the blank rendering, and every court, judge, clerk, prosecutor, attorney, agency, service, signature and decision region blank. Two historical objections are closed against these bytes and the third is confirmed still open by its own record and owned by another lane. Three advisories are recorded and none of them changes what this artifact does.

historicalObjections.originalObjection: protection established by geometry where required, not label alone
historicalObjections.reviewerFinding: The mechanism exists and fires: the current map records protected_page_region refusals carrying a regionHeading, so region is genuinely an input to decideBinding. The prior provenAgainstThisFamilysBytes flag was not taken on trust; it was rechecked against the map and artifact at this commit. However the geometry feeding it is unsound — see WCB-B-REGION-ATTRIBUTION. The objection is closed as to 'region is an input' and not closed as to 'protection established by geometry' being correct.

refuseWhen guards are present on participant.street_address, participant.city, participant.phone and participant.full_legal_name in the shared semantics module, and the current bytes bear it out: name, street and city each appear exactly once, each in its own declared rectangle, and no value appears in a second field. Rechecked directly, not taken from the flag.

The emission half is satisfied: the committed sidecar carries 24 fields with no nulls, and its pins for the canonical artifact, the boundary artifact, the contact sheet, the field map and the classification all match the bytes on disk. The verification half is still open: scripts/verify-rcap-shared-pdf-contract.mjs regenerates a sidecar through artifactProvenance() and asserts against that, so it still never opens a committed sidecar. The record's own 'open' status is accurate; this reviewer confirms it rather than closing it.

advisories.severity: systemic; no wrong outcome in this family
advisories.observation: regionHeading and effectiveLabel are attributed across columns and across rows, so the protection decision is often made on text that does not belong to the field. The name/street/city block is one column at x≈37 width 278, and its three widgets take three different headings, each a line of the form's title block in the adjacent column. effectiveLabel is a whole caption row rather than a field's own caption: PetitionerState, PetitionerZip, DriversLicenseState, Race and Sex all carry the identical label 'Drivers License No.StateRaceSex', which is why PetitionerZip and NameAtty are refused as 'race' and DOB and CityAtty as 'money'.
advisories.whyItIsNotABlockerHere: every one of these misfires is fail-closed. In this family the values that matter are all bound, all correctly placed, and every protected region is blank — proved geometrically and then looked at, not taken from the classification. The recorded refusal reasons are untrue, which misinforms a reader of the map, but it costs this artifact nothing.
advisories.whyItStillMatters: PROTECT_RULES order means an accidental early match ('money', 'race') pre-empts the correct later rule. On AOC-CR-296 the same mechanism fails in the direction that costs the participant data. Fixing it is a wave-level correction, not a family one.
advisories.smallestCorrection: Constrain region attribution to headings whose horizontal extent overlaps the widget's column, and caption attribution to the widget's own cell rather than the whole row. Re-derive the maps and re-render.

advisories.severity: documented behaviour, recorded for the owner
advisories.observation: When a value cannot fit its rectangle at the minimum font size the renderer refuses it rather than clipping, and records the refusal as unfittable_refused_not_clipped. On AOC-CR-287 the boundary fixture drops FileNumber1 entirely: requiredWidthAtMin 118 against a 73pt rectangle. The canonical fixture fits at 68.9pt in the same 73pt cell, so the margin is thin.
advisories.whyItIsNotABlockerHere: the stated approval criteria forbid clipping, truncation and unreadable fitting. Refusing to draw is none of those, it is fail-safe, and the family's own overflow report names every instance.
advisories.whyItStillMatters: a participant with a long case number gets a blank charge-table cell and no notice that anything was withheld.
advisories.smallestCorrection: surface refused-for-width values to the participant, or allow the cell to wrap.

advisories.severity: minor recorded defect in the committed census and map
advisories.observation: FileNumber1's effectiveLabel is stored as "File No.(s)" followed by an undecoded font-encoded run that reads 'Offense Description'. The same failure appears in the DateOfBirth/DOB caption row on AOC-CR-287 and AOC-CR-288.
advisories.whyItIsNotABlockerHere: FileNumber1 was bound on its field name, and 24-CR-001234 is correctly placed inside its rectangle.
advisories.whyItStillMatters: an undecoded caption cannot match any protect rule, so a protected caption that fails to decode protects nothing.
advisories.smallestCorrection: apply the font's ToUnicode mapping when harvesting printed captions in the census, then re-derive the maps.
